summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement and variceal bleeding, was admitted for post-procedure monitoring after undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of two liver tumors and a 4.5-liter paracentesis. He tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complications or evidence of bleeding. Post-procedure imaging revealed a new nonocclusive thrombus in the right axillary vein, which was evaluated with ultrasound. Due to recent bleeding risk, anticoagulation was not initiated, and management will be discussed with his specialist. His medications were continued, including those for hepatic encephalopathy and ascites, and he was discharged home the following day in stable condition with instructions to follow up on labs and the venous clot.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Acute embolism and thrombosis of right axillary vein
